newsitem.title: MEXICO: PRI hardliner sees tragedy if Mexican right wins.
newsitem.headline: PRI hardliner sees tragedy if Mexican right wins.

text.p: A leading hardliner in Mexico's ruling party has warned of a "national tragedy" if conservatives win the country's congressional elections next month, Excelsior newspaper reported on Thursday.

Manuel Bartlett, the governor of Puebla state and a former Interior Minister, told Mexican columnists at a private meeting Wednesday that the ruling Institutional Revolutionary Party (PRI) faced defeat because it had lost credibility and become too bureaucratic, it said.

"Right-wing politics will result in a national tragedy which will encourage ungovernability," Excelsior quoted Bartlett as saying in a reference to the possibility, shown in polls, that conservative gains will rob the PRI of its majority in the lower house of congress for the first time.
The PRI, Bartlett added, "must revise its policies without demagogy, without populism and considering as a priority the social needs of the country".
Bartlett is prominent among the party's old guard who have resisted moves towards free-market economics and greater democracy promoted by President Ernesto Zedillo.

Bartlett told the columnists that free-market economics risked causing a permanent split in the country between haves and have-nots. A victory by the conservative National Action Party (PAN) would amount to a "counter-revolution", he said.
The PRI, born out of the turmoil following the 1910-17 Mexican Revolution, has governed Mexico for the past 68 years, dominating the presidency, congress and state governorships.
Bartlett said the ruling party had declined because it had taken its members for granted and lost touch with the grass roots.
